name: Jordan
fact: Carved directly into vibrant red sandstone cliffs over two millennia ago, the ancient Nabataean city of Petra remains one of the world's most breathtaking architectural wonders.

name: Kazakhstan
fact: Genetic studies confirm that Kazakhstan's wild apple forests in the Tian Shan mountains are the ancestral origin of all domesticated apple varieties enjoyed across the globe today.

name: Kuwait
fact: Stretching over thirty-six kilometers across Kuwait Bay, the remarkable Sheikh Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah Causeway ranks among the world's longest and most advanced vehicular sea bridge networks.

name: Kyrgyzstan
fact: Surrounded by snow-capped Tian Shan peaks, the crystal-clear waters of Lake Issyk-Kul never freeze during winter, earning this magnificent alpine jewel the title of Central Asia's warm lake.

name: Laos
fact: Nestled along the Mekong River, the UNESCO-listed ancient town of Luang Prabang gracefully blends historic Buddhist temples with lush tropical landscapes and vibrant artisan traditions.

name: Lebanon
fact: The breathtaking subterranean limestone caverns of Jeita Grotto showcase magnificent stalactite formations spanning nearly nine kilometers, creating one of the world's most spectacular natural cave systems.

name: Malaysia
fact: Estimated at over one hundred and thirty million years old, Taman Negara flourishes as one of the planet's oldest continuous primary tropical rainforests, harboring exceptional biodiversity.

name: Maldives
fact: Designated as a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, Baa Atoll hosts world-renowned seasonal gatherings of hundreds of graceful manta rays feeding in the nutrient-rich waters of Hanifaru Bay.

name: Mongolia
fact: Dedicated international conservation efforts successfully reintroduced the endangered Przewalski's horse, known locally as the takhi, to roam freely across Mongolia's sweeping native steppes.

name: Myanmar
fact: Across the lush central plains of Bagan, more than three thousand ancient Buddhist temples and pagodas create one of Asia's most spectacular archaeological landscapes.

name: Nepal
fact: Eight of the world's fourteen highest mountain peaks rise within Nepal's dramatic Himalayan terrain, including the majestic summit of Mount Everest.

name: North Korea
fact: Perched in a volcanic crater atop Mount Paektu, the pristine waters of Heaven Lake form one of the highest and deepest alpine crater lakes in the world.

name: Oman
fact: Dating back more than two thousand years, Oman's UNESCO-recognized aflaj irrigation systems utilize gravity to deliver mountain spring water sustainably to desert farming communities.

name: Pakistan
fact: The artisan city of Sialkot manufactures over seventy percent of the world's hand-stitched soccer balls, including the official match balls used in premier FIFA World Cup tournaments.

name: Palestine
capital: Ramallah (administrative seat; Jerusalem is the proclaimed capital)
fact: Celebrated on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list, the traditional folk embroidery known as Tatreez weaves intricate cross-stitch patterns that preserve centuries of vibrant regional storytelling.
